Subject: Role placement guidance — manager track vs senior IC for Jordan Miles

Team,

We need a quick alignment on level/title for Jordan Miles (final on-site + hiring loop next week). Recruiting is asking whether we will extend a Manager title (people manager, L5) or offer a Senior IC (L5 senior individual contributor) and how we want to anchor comp. High-level context: Jordan has been a senior engineering lead at a mid-stage ML infra startup for ~4 years, led a team of 5 engineers for 18 months, owns roadmap for a small infra product, strong cross-functional impact. Interview feedback attached in the loop.

Decision points I need by EOD Monday so People Ops can prepare the offer:
- Level & title: L5 Manager (Manager, people leader) vs L5 Senior IC (senior TPM-style IC)
- Compensation anchor: recommend base / equity / sign-on range (we should be within the published L5 band)
- Any preconditions (e.g., hiring manager confirmation of direct report structure / P&L ownership)

My thinking: scope looks closer to manager (has direct reports + roadmap ownership). If we classify as Manager L5, suggested anchor: base $210k, target equity 0.6% (4-year), sign-on $25k — all within the mid-upper L5 band given West Coast market. If we go Senior IC, base $225k + 0.5% equity, lower sign-on.

Attachments: interview matrix (inline) and I uploaded a quick comp comparator (comp_comparator_q1_2027.xlsx).

Thanks — please reply with brief callouts.

—Olga
Engineering Hiring Partner

On Sun, Mar 14, 2027 at 09:12, Olga Petrov wrote:
> Team,
> 
> We need a quick alignment on level/title for Jordan Miles...

Quick note from leveling standpoint:
- Based on our leveling rubric, the key differentiator for Manager vs Senior IC at L5 is clear scope for people management + consistent track record of coaching/mentoring and doing people-related responsibilities (~12+ months managing direct reports is a soft minimum). Jordan meets that criterion (5 reports for ~18 months).
- The cross-functional ownership described (roadmap + stakeholder alignment across infra and product) is consistent with L5 Manager expectations.
- Interview loop shows strong leadership signals in behavioral + execution, but I want a short follow-up question for the hiring manager on scope of hiring next 12 months (does the role expand to 8+ reports or remain a 3–6 IC team?).

Recommendation: Offer as L5 Manager. Anchor as follows (People Ops-friendly rounding):
- Base: $205,000 — places us in the lower-mid of L5 Manager band but leaves room for performance-based increases.
- Target equity (grant): 0.45% — 4-year, 1-year cliff; recommend small increase at next comp cycle based on impact.
- Sign-on: $20,000 — given internal equity and comp comparator; can be increased to $30k if counter is strong.

I attached my comp comparator extract (comp_comparator_q1_2027.xlsx) with market picks and a suggested final offer line that keeps internal parity with similar hires (see row "L5 Manager - infra lead").

Next step: If everyone agrees, Laura can confirm headcount/manager-level budget and I'll route a draft offer to People Ops for review (I can draft the language for the people-manager responsibilities).

—Marissa
Dir, Talent & Recruiting
Redwood Inference

2) Compensation comps: the suggested base $205k + 0.45% eq + $20k sign-on looks fine vs comp table, but please confirm that it won't create a >10% delta vs peer managers in the same org (we should avoid compression).
